prompt.en: A dummy load is rated for 90 W for 30 seconds, or 35 W continuously. A 70 W test will last two minutes. Which plan respects the stated ratings?

text.en: Run the full test because 70 W is below the 90 W rating.

feedback.en: The 90 W rating has a 30-second limit. It does not cover a two-minute run.

text.en: Run the test while the case feels cool; the short-term rating applies until it feels hot.

feedback.en: Case temperature can lag internal heating. Touch does not replace the power and time ratings.

text.en: Lower power to at most the continuous rating, or use a load rated for the full test.

feedback.en: The planned time exceeds the short-term limit. Use the continuous rating or a load specified for that power and duration.

text.en: Run for two minutes, then allow two minutes off to meet a 50 % duty cycle.

feedback.en: An assumed rest period does not authorize exceeding the stated single-run limit. Follow the actual cooling and duty-cycle instructions.

explanation.en: A dummy load turns RF into heat. Match the test power and duration to its actual continuous, short-run, and cooling specifications.

prompt.en: A block diagram connects microphone audio directly to a frequency multiplier in an FM transmitter. Which correction follows the signal types?

text.en: Feed the multiplier from the oscillator path; route speech through the speech amplifier and modulator.

feedback.en: The multiplier handles oscillator-path RF. The speech path controls the modulator, which varies oscillator frequency in this simplified chain.

text.en: Feed the multiplier from the microphone path; the final amplifier can turn that audio into RF.

feedback.en: An RF power amplifier raises RF power. It does not create the missing modulated carrier from microphone audio.

text.en: Use the multiplier to set audio loudness; feed the oscillator straight to the antenna.

feedback.en: Multiplication changes RF frequency, not microphone loudness. The transmitter still needs modulation and RF power amplification.

text.en: Put speech after the RF power amplifier; keep the oscillator frequency fixed during voice.

feedback.en: In this FM chain, speech controls frequency before multiplication and power amplification. Adding it after the final amplifier bypasses that job.

explanation.en: Signal type determines block placement. Speech controls modulation; the frequency multiplier and power amplifier handle the resulting RF.

prompt.en: A receiver uses a 10.700 MHz IF and a high-side oscillator for a 144.390 MHz signal. Its injection filter passes 154 to 156 MHz. Which oscillator setting fits?

feedback.en: Subtracting the IF gives low-side injection. The stated design uses an oscillator above the signal.
This leaves no frequency difference to produce the stated IF. Add the IF for high-side injection.
This adds the IF twice. One IF separates the desired signal and its local oscillator.
144.390 + 10.700 = 155.090 MHz. It is above the signal and inside the stated pass range.

explanation.en: For high-side injection, the oscillator is one IF above the wanted signal. Check the result against the injection filter range.
